title: Clapping the beats in a word
examples: How many beats are in banana?

explain.say: Words have beats. Each beat is called a syllable. Look at the word banana on the board. You will clap once for each beat.

draw.text: Clapping the beats in a word

explain.say: Look at the first beat: ba. Clap once. Put your hand under your chin and say ba. Your chin drops once for each beat.
Look at the next beat: na. Clap again. Your chin drops again. That is 2 beats so far.
Look at the last beat: na. Clap once more. Banana has 3 beats: ba, na, na. So banana has 3 syllables.
Long words are easier to read in beats. Look at the word elephant. Clap el, e, phant. That is 3 beats. Today, clap the beats in your own name.

faq.a: A syllable is one beat in a word. Cat has one beat. Banana has three.
Clap as you say the word, or put your hand under your chin. Each time your chin drops, that is one beat.
asks: How many beats are in a word?

faq.q: Why does clapping help me read?
faq.a: Long words can look hard. Clapping splits them into small beats. You can read small beats one at a time.

faq.q: Does every syllable have a vowel?
faq.a: Almost always. Every beat has a vowel sound, made by a, e, i, o or u, and sometimes y, like in my.

faq.q: What can I do instead of clapping?
faq.a: You can stamp, jump, tap the table or tap your fingers. Any move works, as long as you make one move for each beat.
asks: Can I stamp instead of clap?

facts: Every syllable has a vowel sound.
Banana and elephant both have three syllables.

quiz.say: Clap the word elephant. How many beats does it have?
quiz.why: El, e, phant: 3 claps, so elephant has 3 syllables.

wrong.0: Clap it again: el, e, phant gives 3 claps.
wrong.2: Elephant has 3 beats, one for each vowel sound.

quiz.say: Clap each word. Which word has 1 beat?
quiz.why: You say dog with 1 clap, so it has 1 beat.

wrong.0: Ti-ger has 2 beats, so you clap twice.
wrong.1: Piz-za has 2 beats, so you clap twice.
